method: Manual inspection of raw-osm.json, raw-overture.json, raw-overture-scored.json. For multi-branch businesses with no branch hint, any genuine branch counts as top-1 correct (branch_ok). Cases where the intended venue is absent from the underlying dataset are marked ABSENT so coverage failures are separable from ranking failures.

verdict_key.OK: top-1 is the intended venue (or a genuine branch of it); for NEG cases, nothing was auto-accepted
verdict_key.TOP3: intended venue present in results but not at rank 1
verdict_key.MISS_RANK: intended venue exists in the dataset but was not returned in the top 3
verdict_key.MISS_NONAME: correct coordinates returned but with no usable name, so unpresentable
verdict_key.ABSENT: intended venue verified absent from the underlying dataset (see overpass-coverage*.json / probe output) - a coverage failure, not a ranking failure
verdict_key.FALSE_POSITIVE: a confident but wrong POI returned for a query that names no venue

notes: overture_scored OK verdicts for NEG-01..03 mean the top candidate scored below the auto-accept band and was therefore routed to the confirm/no-match UI, not silently saved. The raw top-1 names were wrong in all three cases.

TLV-04 Imperial Craft Cocktail Bar, TLV-08 Orna and Ella, TLV-09 Cafe Xoho: verified ABSENT from OpenStreetMap by Overpass name-regex over any name:* key in a Tel Aviv bbox. TLV-04 and TLV-09 are PRESENT in Overture. TLV-02 Cafe Levinsky 41 is present in OSM (as name:en only, no name tag) and absent from Overture. The datasets have complementary gaps.
LDN-08 Dishoom Shoreditch is present in OSM as way/276329431 name=Dishoom addr:street=Boundary Street; Nominatim returned zero results for it. That is a search-engine failure, not a data failure.
